recipes.name: Fix wasm32 memory with -C link-arg=--no-growable-memory or equal, page-aligned --initial-memory/--max-memory
recipes.what: On rustc 1.98.1 (rust-lld, LLD 22.1.8) two stable link args make a wasm32 module's maximum equal its initial size; memory.grow of one page then returns -1 on every host.
recipes.how: Pass -C link-arg=--no-growable-memory (the maximum becomes the initial size wasm-ld computes: 1 MiB stack, data, statics, rounded up to pages) or -C link-arg=--initial-memory=N -C link-arg=--max-memory=N with N a multiple of 65,536 and at least the bytes wasm-ld reports. RUSTFLAGS replaces the [target] rustflags of .cargo/config.toml, so put the argument where it survives: a build.rs printing cargo::rustc-link-arg-cdylib=--no-growable-memory (measured: still 18/18 pages with RUSTFLAGS set), or repeat it in every RUSTFLAGS. Check the result with a decoder: memory limits flag 0x01 with max == min. From Rust, core::arch::wasm32::memory_grow(0, n) returns usize::MAX (-1 as i32) once the maximum would be exceeded.
recipes.gotchas: wasm-ld refuses, verbatim: 'initial memory must be aligned to the page size (65536 bytes)', 'initial memory too small, 1117808 bytes needed' (for the solver), 'maximum memory too small, 4194304 bytes needed' (max below initial). --no-growable-memory alone fixes the memory at the linker's minimum (18 pages for the solver), leaving std's allocator about 60 KB of heap: the product golden printed NAN and 32 of 73 tests failed. The link args change only the memory section; std's allocator keeps its memory.grow instruction (see the fixed-arena allocator recipe). No -Z flag is needed.
recipes.engine_note: solver/build.mjs (RUSTFLAGS) and solver/.cargo/config.toml, T3 pin 2. Measured on a copy of solver/: no args gives initial 18 pages and no maximum; --no-growable-memory gives 18/18; --initial-memory = --max-memory = 4194304 gives 64/64; the memory.grow count stays 1 in all three. PR #44 fixes 256 pages with the two explicit args in both config.toml and build.mjs.

recipes.name: Remove memory.grow from the law's binary with a fixed-arena #[global_allocator]: dlmalloc 0.2.13 over one span
recipes.what: std 1.98.1's wasm32 System allocator is dlmalloc 0.2.13 and calls memory.grow; a #[global_allocator] that hands dlmalloc one fixed span removes the instruction and left the solver's results bit-identical.
recipes.how: Add dlmalloc = "=0.2.13" and a static Dlmalloc<Arena> built with Dlmalloc::new_with_allocator(Arena { .. }). Arena implements the unsafe trait dlmalloc::Allocator: alloc hands out one span once (a zero-initialised static array, or __heap_base up to memory_size(0) * 65536 under fixed memory) and returns (null, 0, 0) after that; remap returns null; free_part, free and can_release_part return false; allocates_zeros returns true; page_size returns 65536. Forward GlobalAlloc alloc, alloc_zeroed, dealloc and realloc to malloc, calloc, free and realloc, mark the static #[global_allocator], and link with --no-growable-memory or equal initial and max. Size the span from the high-water mark of a growable build (memory.buffer.byteLength after the heaviest run): dlmalloc never releases and wasm memory never shrinks.
recipes.gotchas: Linker limits alone keep the instruction: the fixed-memory builds still contain one memory.grow in <dlmalloc::sys::System as dlmalloc::Allocator>::alloc. dlmalloc 0.2.13 donates the linker's __heap_base..__heap_end span only on its first system request and forfeits it if that request does not fit (src/wasm.rs 39-48). Exhaustion returns null and Rust aborts: an unreachable trap, identical on every host once max == initial. The heap need scales with contacts, not bodies: 49, 147 and 3,320 pages for a settling pile, a dense stack and an all-overlapping world at the same 64/64/256 caps under today's law; 53, 245 and 3,973 under PR #44's per-quantum rebuild.
recipes.engine_note: solver/src/lib.rs (#[global_allocator]) and solver/Cargo.toml, T3 pins 2 and 8. Measured on a copy: dlmalloc over a 32 MiB arena gives 532/532 pages and 0 memory.grow, and goldens fd2f6c03fb982d77 / 0d38671370d12d1e and 73/73 tests are unchanged; the product harness needs 21 pages today. PR #44's src/arena.rs rebuilt here also has 0 memory.grow, but its dense capacity scene peaks at 245 of its 256 pages; 512 pages leaves about 2x.

recipes.name: Lint wasm by decoding every instruction: 0x40 and 0xFD bytes recur in block types, immediates and data
recipes.what: The solver binary's code section holds 16,558 bytes equal to 0x40 against one memory.grow (14,916 of them empty block types) and 277 bytes equal to 0xFD against zero SIMD instructions; i32.const 32893 encodes as 41 fd 80 02.
recipes.how: Walk sections by id and u32 size. In the code section read each body's size, skip its locals vector, then decode instruction by instruction with a table that knows every immediate: block types (0x40, a one-byte value type, or an s33 index), br_table vectors, memarg with the bit-6 memidx, i32/i64 const as signed LEB128, f32/f64 const as 4/8 bytes, 0xFC and 0xFD sub-opcodes as u32 LEB128, 16 bytes for v128.const and i8x16.shuffle, lane indices. Flag only at opcode positions, and refuse any opcode or sub-opcode the table lacks, so a gap can only cause a false refusal. In Rust, wasmparser's FunctionBody::get_operators_reader() does the decoding.
recipes.gotchas: Scanning the whole file adds data-segment and custom-section bytes; scanning only the code section still misfires, because every block, loop or if without results is 02/03/04 40, i32.const -64 is 41 40 and an unpadded index of 64 is the byte 40. A byte-level over-approximation that refuses any 0x40 or 0xFD refuses the pinned binary. The target_features custom section (+relaxed-simd, +simd128) is a cheap second signal, but custom sections are optional.
recipes.engine_note: solver/lint.mjs and solver/lint.test.js, T3 pins 2 and 3. PR #44's lint.mjs decodes this way; run on hand-assembled modules it accepted the four false-positive cases and refused the real ones. Two gaps that do not touch rustc output: 0xFD sub-opcodes below 0x100 missing from its table pass as immediate-free, and table.grow is not refused.

recipes.name: Match relaxed SIMD as 0xFD then u32 LEB128 256..=275 and memory.grow as 0x40 then a memidx, padding allowed
recipes.what: Relaxed SIMD is 0xFD followed by the opcode 0x100..=0x113 as a u32 LEB128 (canonically fd 80 02 to fd 93 02; 0x114-0x12F reserved) and memory.grow is 0x40 followed by a memidx; V8 and wasmparser accept padded encodings such as fd 80 82 80 80 00 and 40 80 00.
recipes.how: After an opcode byte 0xFD read the sub-opcode as an unsigned LEB128 of up to 5 bytes (the fifth carries 4 value bits) and refuse 256 <= sub <= 275. After 0x40 read a u32 LEB128 memidx instead of expecting the byte 0x00. For each defined or imported memory read the limits flag: 0x00 (min only) is growable, 0x01 needs max == min, 0x04/0x05 are the i64 address type and 0x02/0x03 shared; refuse what the law must not produce.
recipes.gotchas: A byte-pattern search for fd 80 02 misses a padded encoding, which the spec allows up to ceil(N/7) bytes (0x03 and 0x83 0x00 both encode 3). 0x114 is not a relaxed opcode: V8 rejects the module and wasmparser reports 'unknown 0xfd subopcode: 0x114'. The spec's own instruction index was cut off before SIMD when retrieved; the numbered list is the relaxed-simd proposal's table.
recipes.engine_note: T3 pin 2 ('the 0xfd prefix with opcodes 0x100 through 0x113') and PR #44's lint.mjs constants RELAXED_SIMD_FIRST/LAST and MEMORY_GROW. Add to solver/lint.test.js: i32.const 32893 (41 fd 80 02) and an empty block, accepted; fd 80 82 80 80 00 and 40 80 00, refused.

recipes.name: Don't rely on -C target-feature=-relaxed-simd: a #[target_feature] fn or a relaxed intrinsic still emits
recipes.what: Under -C target-feature=-relaxed-simd a #[target_feature(enable = "relaxed-simd")] function and a plain call to core::arch::wasm32::f32x4_relaxed_madd both compile without unsafe and emit f32x4.relaxed_madd (fd 85 02).
recipes.how: Keep the crate-level -C target-feature=-relaxed-simd: it sets cfg(target_feature = "relaxed-simd") for every crate built, which is what gates the relaxed paths in matrixmultiply 0.3.11 (sgemm muladd becomes f32x4_relaxed_madd) and wide 1.7.1 (u8x16::shuffle becomes u8x16_relaxed_swizzle). Make the binary lint the guarantee, and when adding a dependency grep it for target_feature(enable and for *_relaxed_* intrinsics.
recipes.gotchas: The rustc book: there is no compiler flag that disables SIMD emission once a function enables it with #[target_feature]. On Wasm a safe #[target_feature] fn is callable from safe code, so the call site carries no unsafe marker. The precompiled std is built with the target's default features and ignores -C target-feature. relaxed-simd implies simd128. relaxed_madd may round once or twice depending on the host.
recipes.engine_note: solver/.cargo/config.toml, solver/build.mjs and FLAGS.md: the flag holds for today's graph (0 SIMD instructions in the binary) but is not the guarantee; T3 pin 2's lint is. PR #44's config.toml comment already says this.

recipes.name: Expect Rapier 0.35.3 to stop T4's fast box at a fixed slab with ccd_enabled(false); max_ccd_substeps 0 tunnels
recipes.what: In rapier3d-f64 0.35.3 every dynamic body moving more than half its thinnest half-extent per step is swept against fixed colliders even with ccd_enabled(false); ccd_enabled(true) only adds kinematic and dynamic targets.
recipes.how: IntegrationParameters::max_ccd_substeps is the switch: 1 (the default) sweeps fast dynamic bodies against fixed colliders and clamps next_position to the first time of impact, 0 disables all CCD. RigidBodyBuilder::ccd_enabled(true) makes a bullet that also sweeps kinematic and dynamic bodies, never another bullet. Fast means max point velocity * dt > 0.5 * ccd_thickness, and a cuboid's ccd_thickness is its smallest half-extent: a 0.05 box at dt = 1/64 is fast above 1.6 u/s. To show a tunnelling test failing, run it with max_ccd_substeps = 0.
recipes.gotchas: The clamp moves the pose only; velocities are kept and the next step's speculative contacts absorb the approach. A body already overlapping a target is not clamped in 3D (only fractions > 0 are accepted). Non-bullets never sweep moving bodies, bullets never sweep bullets, heightfield targets are one-sided, and mesh-shaped fast bodies are never swept. Linear speed is capped at 400 u/s per substep. Pre-0.35 advice that CCD is off unless ccd_enabled no longer holds. Measured envelope at dt 1/64: no tunnelling for 1 to 1,000 u/s against fixed slabs of half-thickness 0.02 to 0.0001.
recipes.engine_note: T4 pin 2 and its acceptance line: rapier_law.rs build_world makes dynamic bodies with ccd_enabled(false) and inherits max_ccd_substeps = 1, so the fast-body test already passes. Through solver_step 14/14 start phases stay on the near side, a copy with max_ccd_substeps = 0 tunnels in 10/14, and ccd_enabled(true) left every result identical; it only adds sweeps against the kinematic walker.

recipes.name: Set T4's step heights around max_height + offset: KinematicCharacterController climbs 0.31 at max_height 0.3
recipes.what: handle_stairs evaluates max_height + offset and min_width + offset, so with max_height 0.3 and offset 0.01 the engine's box walker climbs steps up to 0.3101, and its feet rest one offset above every surface.
recipes.how: Autostep runs only on a wall hit (angle to up >= max_slope_climb_angle) and, with include_dynamic_bodies = false, never onto a collider whose parent is dynamic (the step casts then exclude dynamic bodies). It needs a free up-cast of max_height + offset, a free forward cast of min_width + offset from the raised pose, and a landing no steeper than the climb angle (strict >). Put the course pair clear of max_height + offset, e.g. 0.29 and 0.33, and measure feet as y - hy - offset.
recipes.gotchas: Asserting the feet at the step top within 1e-3 fails by the 0.01 skin. The limit barely moves with speed: 0.3100989 at 0.4 u/s, 0.3100939 at 2 u/s. Relative lengths evaluate against the shape's AABB (height, or for min_width the horizontal diagonal); the engine uses Absolute. The current Rapier guide says autostep needs floor contact first; the pinned 0.35.3 code does not check that.
recipes.engine_note: harness/course.test.js, T4 pin 5: rapier_law.rs controller() sets STEP_HEIGHT 0.3, STEP_MIN_WIDTH 0.2 and SKIN 0.01. Through solver_step with the product walker (0.25 box) a 0.31 step is climbed, 0.311 is not, and the stopped walker waits 0.0101 short of the riser.

recipes.name: Keep T4 slope and ledge cases off the controller's comparisons: >= at 45 degrees, nudge creep, speed-set snap
recipes.what: is_wall is angle >= max_slope_climb_angle and is_nonslip_slope is angle <= min_slope_slide_angle; snap needs a grounded start and translation.up <= 0; the 1e-4 normal nudge lifts a walker blocked on a 46 degree slope by about 6e-5 per quantum; the snap-or-fall threshold moves with speed (0.2105, 0.2097, 0.2058 at 0.4, 1, 2 u/s).
recipes.how: Test slopes at 44 and 46 degrees with the speed and quantum count stated: at 2 u/s 46 degrees gains 0.018 by 320 quanta and 0.038 by 640 while 44 degrees reaches the top; never test exactly 45. Test drops at 0.19 and 0.22: 0.19 has a longest ungrounded run of at most 1 and lands within 2 quanta of clearing the edge, and 0.22 falls for 12 quanta at 0.4, 1 and 2 u/s. Snap casts down snap_to_ground with offset as target distance, and only when move_shape started grounded (a contact within offset + 0.05 with normal.up >= 1e-3).
recipes.gotchas: Exactly 45 degrees is a wall (>=) but its landing check is strict (>), and the walker creeps up (0.169 in 160 quanta at 2 u/s). The 46 degree 'gain below 0.05' holds only for bounded runs: 0.077 by 1,280 quanta, 0.61 by 10,000. A 0.21 drop is snapped at 0.4 u/s, the product walker's speed, after sliding down the corner while counted grounded, but falls for 12 quanta at 2 u/s; at 0.4 and 2 u/s the quantum that clears the edge is ungrounded for every drop. normal_nudge_factor = 0 removes the creep, but the walker then climbs nothing. Past a ramp's top the walker walks off and its end height drops back to the floor, so assert the maximum height or give the ramp a landing.
recipes.engine_note: harness/course.test.js, T4 pin 5, and rapier_law.rs controller() (CLIMB_ANGLE pi/4, SLIDE_ANGLE 50 degrees, SNAP 0.2, normal_nudge_factor 1e-4); integrate() zeroes vy on movement.grounded, which is how a test reads 'grounded' from the body record.

recipes.name: Allow ~1,200 quanta for a walker started 0.1 inside the floor: Rapier depenetrates only on a zero desired move
recipes.what: move_shape runs its depenetration pass only for a zero desired translation, and the engine always passes gravity, so a walker started 0.1 inside the floor rises only by the 1e-4 normal nudge per quantum and stands after about 1,200 quanta.
recipes.how: Assert the recovery over a stated run instead of an instant fix: over at least 1,300 quanta the feet end at the floor plus the offset and never go below their start (measured -0.0936 at quantum 64, -0.0360 at 640, +0.0101 at 1,280).
recipes.gotchas: The depenetration pass, when it does run, is capped at a quarter of the character's height per call. With normal_nudge_factor = 0 the walker stays 0.1 inside indefinitely. The trace was the same at vx 0 and 0.4.
recipes.engine_note: harness/course.test.js, T4 pin 5 ('a walker starting with its centre inside the floor by 0.1 ends standing on the floor'): rapier_law.rs integrate() always passes (vx, vy + G*DT, vz) * DT, so the depenetration branch never runs for a driven walker.
